top: finished steel imports in April–August 2026, to 3.49 million tonnes, with a safeguard duty in force.
safeguard duty on flat steel since 21 April 2026; domestic producers have asked for more than 20%.

sections.h2: Demand grew faster than output as imports and exports both jumped

chart.title: Steel consumption rose 7.4%, faster than finished steel output at 4.1%
chart.source: Joint Plant Committee provisional data, as reported in October 2026.

sections.means: Consumption outran output, so the import gap reflects demand as well as the duty.
sections.todo: Compare the April–October figures with the April–August base before reading the 29.5% rise as a trend.

sections.h2: The duty steps down half a point a year, but its exemptions are not measured

chart.title: The duty falls from 12% to 11.5% now and to 11% from April 2027
chart.sub: Safeguard duty on flat steel, per cent, by year from 21 April.
chart.source: Gazette of India, Notification No. 02/2025-Customs (SG), 30 December 2025.

sections.means: The duty is a 12% to 11% schedule, and its CIF-price and developing-country exemptions mean the share of imports paying it is unknown.
sections.todo: Ask for the published share of dutiable imports before judging how much the duty has held back the 3.49 million tonnes.

sections.h2: Registration and quality-order rules decide who imports, and get less attention

chart.title: The open houses cover registration and quality orders, not the duty
chart.source: Ministry of Steel PIB releases; CBIC Circular 23/2026-Customs; trade press as reported.
